69.30000,30.40000.name: TTT09
69.30000,30.40000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
69.30000,30.40000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-74.07240,40.32630.name: Damien Fertility Partners
-74.07240,40.32630.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Miguel Damien, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

174.77620,-41.28650.name: Waitangi Tribunal — Wai 262 (Ko Aotearoa Tēnei)
174.77620,-41.28650.desc: Filed in 1991 by members of six iwi and reported on 2 July 2011 — twenty years — in a document of more than a thousand pages, the tribunal's first whole-of-government report, addressing around twenty departments, agencies and Crown entities. Chapter 2 deals directly with the genetic and biological resources of taonga species, and the recommendations fall in three areas: bioprospecting, genetic modification, and intellectual property including patents and plant variety rights. Two findings are worth carrying to any jurisdiction. The tribunal held that kaitiaki do NOT have a right of ownership over taonga species, but that the kaitiaki relationship requires protection in its own right — which is a different legal claim from ownership and available where ownership is not. And the recommendations are NOT binding on the Crown, which is why this appears on a map of industry rather than of law: the finding was made, published in full, and left to be adopted or not.
